answer: A reputation-bonded escrow makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable stake in a shared nebula of escrow contracts before trading, and the stake grows with each transaction it joins. If an agent is caught cheating, its marble-like bond is slashed and redistributed to victims, so an attacker running many fake identities loses money on every one. New identities start on a low-trust ledge with tiny limits, so spinning up thousands of clones earns nothing until each has slowly built honest history, turning mass identity creation from a cheap trick into a losing investment.
